samples.summary: mergeSelection's new re-spill can write spill ghosts into a merged block, and setCell normalizes them onto the merge anchor (overwriting it)
samples.evidence: mergeSelection now consumes blockers (line 4452) and re-queues the anchor via recalculateWithUnblocked (4461) AFTER setMerge/rebuildMergeCoverMap (4457-4459). The anchor then re-spills into cells that are now merge-covered. calculator.ts:141 writes ghosts with sheet.setCell(ghostRef, ...), and Sheet.setCell (sheet.ts:954) does store.set(this.normalizeRefToAnchor(ref), cell) — so a ghost destined for a covered cell is written to the MERGE ANCHOR cell instead, clobbering whatever the merge anchor held. The new test 'spill re-attempts when merging erases the blocking cell' hits exactly this: A4=MINVERSE spills 2x2 into A4:B5 while B3:B4 is merged, so the B4 ghost lands in B3 (the merge anchor) — the test only asserts A4 and never checks B3. Worse, later cleanup (removeData sheet.ts:1186-1188, calculator.ts:78-82) looks up ghosts with the RAW ref (B4), so the ghost stranded in B3 is never removed: permanently orphaned, read-only content in the merged cell.

samples.summary: Cut-paste still copies spill ghosts to the destination and leaves the source ghosts behind — the exact hazard this delta fixed only for moveRangeTo
samples.evidence: moveRangeTo now skips ghosts when building movedGrid and deletes stale ones (sheet.ts:2386-2390, 2446), documenting that a copied ghost 'reads as user data blocking the anchor's re-spill'. The cut-paste path in the same delta was left untouched: cut() -> fetchGrid copies ghost cells verbatim, relocateGrid (clipboard.ts:28) does newGrid.set(newSref, {...cell}) preserving spillAnchor, and setGrid writes them at the destination as cells carrying a spillAnchor that names a sref which no longer spills there. Meanwhile the source loop at sheet.ts:2259 (`if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue`) leaves the original ghosts in place. Both copies are then read-only forever (setData sheet.ts:1095 returns, removeData sheet.ts:1173 skips, autofill sheet.ts:2692 skips), so the user cannot clear them, and the pasted phantom will block any future spill there.

samples.summary: Drag-moving only a spill anchor (without its ghost cells) orphans the ghosts at the source
samples.evidence: The new ghost handling only drops ghosts that are inside the moved selection (`if (grid.has(cell.spillAnchor)) staleGhosts.add(sref)`, sheet.ts:2388). If the user selects just the anchor cell (e.g. A1 of a MUNIT(2) spill) and drags it, the anchor is moved with its spillRows/spillCols and re-spills at the destination, but the ghosts at B1/A2/B2 still carry spillAnchor='A1'; nothing in moveRangeTo touches cells outside the source range. Those ghosts become permanently unremovable (setData 1095 / removeData 1173 / autofill 2692 all skip cells with spillAnchor) and will block future spills there. The comment at 2380-2382 asserts ghosts 'are dropped at the source and re-created when the anchor re-evaluates', which is only true when the ghosts happen to be inside the dragged range.

samples.summary: Blocker registrations can be keyed on merge-covered srefs that no gesture will ever consume, so the newly added unblock paths cannot fire for them
samples.evidence: calculator.ts:107-110 registers the blocker under the raw sref of the spill position, but the content it read came from sheet.getCell -> normalizeRefToAnchor (sheet.ts:947), i.e. from the merge ANCHOR cell. All the consume sites added in this delta (sheet.ts:2261, 2449, 2696, 4452) look up either the raw sref or the normalized destination sref, never the merge anchor of the recorded blocker. When the blocking content actually lives in a merge anchor, clearing it (setData on the anchor consumes only the anchor's own sref) never consumes the registration keyed on the covered sref, and the spill anchor stays #REF! indefinitely.

verdict.reason: Every link of the claimed chain verified. mergeSelection consumes spill blockers (sheet.ts:4452) and re-queues the anchor via recalculateWithUnblocked (sheet.ts:4461) AFTER setMerge/merges.set/rebuildMergeCoverMap (sheet.ts:4457-4459), so the re-spill runs with the new merge cover map live. calculator.ts:141 writes ghosts with sheet.setCell(ghostRef, ...), and Sheet.setCell normalizes to the merge anchor (sheet.ts:953-955 via normalizeRefToAnchor at 812-814) — so a ghost aimed at a covered cell is stored in the merge ANCHOR, replacing its cell object (dropping any style-only content). The new test (calculation.test.ts:263-282) reproduces this geometry (A4 2x2 spill, merge B3:B4, ghost target B4 -> written to B3) and asserts only A4 at line 281, never B3. The blocker scan also reads through normalized getCell (calculator.ts:107-111), so an empty/style-only anchor is not detected as a blocker and the write proceeds. Cleanup uses raw refs — removeData store.get/delete(ghostRef) (sheet.ts:1185-1189), setData (sheet.ts:1110-1114), and calculator.ts:78-81 deletes via Sheet.deleteCell which is unnormalized store.delete (sheet.ts:967-969) — so the ghost in B3 is never removed. It is then unrecoverable: setData returns early on existing.spillAnchor (sheet.ts:1095) and removeData skips spillAnchor cells (sheet.ts:1173), leaving a permanently read-only, unclearable merged cell holding content the user never entered. No merge-awareness guard exists anywhere in the spill path. Broken invariant + data/style overwrite + orphaned state = critical correctness defect.

verdict.reason: The cut-paste path is present exactly as described and lacks the ghost handling moveRangeTo received. cut() buffers the raw grid (sheet.ts:2151-2158 -> fetchGrid sheet.ts:1897 -> memory.ts:145-157 returns cells verbatim including spillAnchor); relocateGrid copies non-formula cells with `{...cell}` (clipboard.ts:28), preserving an un-relocated spillAnchor; setGrid (sheet.ts:960, memory.ts:137) writes them at the destination. The source loop skips ghosts unconditionally (sheet.ts:2259), so ghosts whose anchor the cut carried away are orphaned in place — the stale-ghost case moveRangeTo now deletes (sheet.ts:2384-2400, 2446). Both the pasted copies and the orphaned source ghosts are permanently uneditable: setData returns (sheet.ts:1095), removeData skips (sheet.ts:1173), autofill skips (sheet.ts:2692), sheet.ts:4214 skips. That is a broken ghost-lifetime invariant with user-visible, unclearable phantom data on a normal cut->paste flow, squarely in the correctness lane. One sub-claim is wrong — calculator.ts:109 does not treat a spillAnchor cell as a blocker and calculator.ts:141 overwrites it — but that only removes the 'blocks future spill' consequence, not the defect.

finding.summary: Drag-moving a range that contains a spill leaves ghost cells behind at the source and duplicates them at the destination with a stale `spillAnchor`
finding.evidence: `movedGrid` is built from `fetchGrid(normalizedSource)`, which returns every stored cell in the range including spill ghosts (`{ v, spillAnchor: <oldAnchorSref> }`); those objects are copied verbatim to the destination (`movedGrid.set(newSref, { ...cell })`, line 2348) so the destination gets ghost cells pointing at an anchor sref that no longer holds that spill. At the same time the source-clear loop does `if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue;` (line 2389), so the original ghosts are *not* deleted from the source. Result: ghost values are visible in two places, and the copies at the destination can never be cleaned up by the calculator (its cleanup only deletes cells whose `spillAnchor === sref` at `anchorRef + offset`). This is in the function this diff modifies and interacts directly with the new spill-blocker bookkeeping (the new `consumeSpillBlocker` calls are skipped for exactly those `continue`d cells); it appears pre-existing rather than introduced here.

verdict.reason: The described code is not present in `moveRangeTo`. (1) Ghosts are never copied to the destination: the build loop at sheet.ts:2386-2400 does `if (cell.spillAnchor) { if (grid.has(cell.spillAnchor)) staleGhosts.add(sref); continue; }` (2387-2390) BEFORE `movedGrid.set(newSref, { ...cell })` (2399), so no cell with a `spillAnchor` ever enters `movedGrid`. The reviewer's cited line 2348 is the `destEnd` computation, not a `movedGrid.set`. (2) The source-clear guard is not the unqualified `if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor) continue;` claimed; at sheet.ts:2446 it reads `if (sourceCell?.spillAnchor && !staleGhosts.has(sref)) continue;`, so ghosts whose anchor moved with the range ARE deleted at the source (2447), added to `changedSrefs` (2448), and passed to `consumeSpillBlocker` (2449). Ghosts whose anchor lies outside the moved range are intentionally preserved because that anchor still owns those positions. The unqualified guard the reviewer quoted exists only at sheet.ts:2259, inside the cut-paste branch of `pasteGrid`, a different function whose grid comes from clipboard content, not `fetchGrid(normalizedSource)` — it has no destination-duplication mechanic and so is not the described defect.
